Women Talking Trailer · Women Talking –.title: Women Talking – Official Trailer
Women Talking Trailer · Women Talking –.body: Trailer for Sarah Polley's 'Women Talking'. Mennonite women secretly gather in a hayloft to decide whether to forgive, stay and fight, or leave after systemic sexual violence by the colony's men. 1:42 long.

Inside Out 2 Clip · Inside Out 2 clip.title: Inside Out 2 clip
Inside Out 2 Clip · Inside Out 2 clip.body: A 14-second trailer clip: Envy gazes in awe at the control console, then Joy, Fear, Disgust and Anger react with shared shock.

themes.name: Coping with Change
themes.description: The theme of coping with change is central to the clip, illustrated by the reactions of the original emotions to a new arrival. The appearance of Envy at the console is an unexpected disruption to their established world. The subsequent shot of Joy, Fear, Anger, and Disgust standing together in shared shock visualizes the struggle and apprehension that comes with adapting to new circumstances, particularly the transition into adolescence.

themes.name: Emotional Complexity
themes.description: This theme is introduced with the arrival of Envy, a new emotion. Unlike the primary emotions of the first film, Envy represents a more nuanced, socially-driven feeling. Her appearance signifies that Riley's inner world is evolving as she gets older, moving beyond basic feelings to more complex ones tied to social comparison and desire. The trailer sets up a narrative about how these new, complicated emotions integrate with—or clash with—the original set.

items.title: Envy
items.subtitle: Ayo Edebiri
items.description: New emotion: tiny, teal-skinned, in purple pajamas, with huge sparkling eyes. She gazes in awe at the console.

items.title: Joy
items.subtitle: Amy Poehler
items.description: Leader of the original emotions, with blue hair and a yellow dress. Her cheer gives way to deep concern.

items.title: Fear
items.subtitle: Tony Hale
items.description: Tall, lanky and purple, in a houndstooth vest and bow tie. He looks shocked on top of his usual nerves.

items.title: Disgust
items.subtitle: Liza Lapira
items.description: Green-skinned, in a green dress and pink scarf. Her usual disdain turns to wide-eyed shock.

items.title: Anger
items.subtitle: Lewis Black
items.description: Short, stout and red, in a white shirt and tie. His fiery manner is replaced by shared confusion.

items.title: Coping with Change
items.description: Envy's arrival disrupts the emotions' established world. Joy, Fear, Disgust and Anger stand together in shared shock, showing the apprehension of adapting to the move into adolescence.

items.title: Emotional Complexity
items.description: Envy is a more nuanced, social emotion tied to comparison and desire. Her arrival suggests Riley's inner world is growing beyond basic feelings.

items.title: Envy reaches for a button
items.subtitle: Envy
items.description: Her star-filled eyes and gentle touch on a blue button show wonder and longing. She wants what the others already hold, which is control of the console.

items.title: Hands clasped, eyes wide
items.subtitle: Fear
items.description: He is nervous as ever, but the terror is amplified. He sees a newcomer as a real threat to Riley's safety.

items.title: Mouth agape, deep concern
items.subtitle: Joy
items.description: Her usual cheer is gone. Joy leads the group and now sees her role being challenged, which shows how much she is shaken.

items.title: Arms crossed, appalled disbelief
items.subtitle: Disgust
items.description: Her crossed arms show judgment and distrust. She reacts to Envy as something she needs to guard against.

items.title: Fists unclenched, stunned silence
items.subtitle: Anger
items.description: Anger doesn't explode, and that is the surprise. Silence from the most volatile emotion shows how big the moment is.

Trailer Comparison · Trailer Comparison.title: Trailer Comparison
Trailer Comparison · Trailer Comparison.subtitle: Women Talking trailer vs Inside Out 2 clip

items.title: Tone
items.subtitle: Somber and urgent vs. playful and curious
items.description: Women Talking: desaturated farmland, voiceover about love and violence, heated debate. Inside Out 2: bright Pixar look, awe turning to comic shock.

items.title: Themes
items.subtitle: Oppression and moral choice vs. growing up
items.description: Women Talking: faith vs. forgiveness, female solidarity, resistance to abuse. Inside Out 2: coping with change, emotional complexity.

items.title: Characters
items.subtitle: Human ensemble vs. emotion ensemble
items.description: Women Talking: Ona, Salome, Mariche, Agata, Scarface Janz, with Autje narrating (Rooney Mara, Claire Foy, Jessie Buckley, Frances McDormand). Inside Out 2: Envy meets Joy, Fear, Anger and Disgust (Ayo Edebiri, Amy Poehler, Tony Hale, Lewis Black, Liza Lapira).

items.title: Pacing
items.subtitle: 102s slow-building vs. 14s two-beat
items.description: Women Talking: four chapters (0-25s, 25-57s, 57-90s, 90-102s), escalating from quiet to confrontation. Inside Out 2: two beats, Envy (0-7s) then the reactions (8-13s), with no dialogue.

items.title: Story-building
items.subtitle: Argument-driven vs. reveal-driven
items.description: Women Talking: philosophical hook, hayloft debate (forgive, fight or leave), trauma flashes, then title and cast. Inside Out 2: a single inciting incident, the arrival of Envy, followed by the reaction shot to set up the conflict.
